Idli is widely praised as a highly nutritious, soft, and fluffy South Indian breakfast staple made from fermented rice and lentil batter. It is consistently rated as a healthy, low-fat, and easily digestible meal, often served with sambar and chutney. It is popular for its high nutritional value and, when served steaming hot, is considered a superior, light, and delicious food choice.
Key Takeaways
Health Benefits: High in protein and fiber, helping with satiety, while fermentation improves digestibility.
Texture & Taste: Exceptionally soft, spongy, and light.
Best Pairings: Commonly enjoyed with hot sambar, coconut chutney, and podi (gunpowder).
Dining Experience: Idli House in Mumbai is often highlighted for serving a wide variety of, sometimes innovative, steamed idlis, such as those served in leaf wrappers, providing a unique dining experience.
Convenience: Ready-to-use batters, such as iD Fresh, are popular and reviewed positively for quality and freshness.
While generally revered, some travelers noted that at high-traffic spots like airports, idlis may occasionally be paired with reheated, less-fresh sides, and service can be inattentive.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are searching for authentic Andhra food in Bandra, Nanna House is a place you should not miss. This South Indian cafe specialises in traditional Andhra cuisine, and the flavours truly reflect home-style cooking. The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

The dosa selection is excellent. The karam podi dosa was spicy, crisp, and full of flavour, while the butter masala dosa was comforting and indulgent. Every dish felt freshly prepared and true to South Indian food traditions, making it one of the better South Indian restaurants in Bandra.

The highlight for me was the putharekulu dessert, a rare Andhra sweet that is difficult to find in Mumbai. Light, ghee-rich, and delicately sweet, it ended the meal beautifully. Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

An Exceptionally Great Breakfast experience for us at this restaurant!

Very neat and tidy but clean place, with only four tables on the ground floor and probably another four on the first floor. Very simple interior and ambience that makes us feel at ease.

Very good service by a very efficient person Tiwari ji who is always on the move and taking care of every person on every table, without a need to call again and remind for anything. A very humble person with smiling face, Tiwari ji caters to all our requests with full energy throughout. He is Occasionally assisted or supported by the owner of the place who supervises all activities, in the kitchen and with the guests alike.

Now, coming to the food part, a really awesome experience I would say.

An humble Upma, tasted so nice, making me to say it was one of the best Upmas I must have eaten outside. Everything was so impeccable with its looks, texture, taste and it was doubly complimented by the Coconut Chutney served alongwith it.

Rasam Vada with Chutney was another great thing to savour, no complaints on it.

The Star of the show was Button Idly with Srilankan Curry -  something I am short of words to appreciate and explain. Sambhar replaced by Coconut based gravy in a bowl and button idlys immersed in them, so that they absorb all the flavours of the gravy within them, each bite of every piece of the Idly kept us craving for more! A very great and unique experience for us.

All this ended with a supurb dose of Filter Coffee, customised to our choice of regular or strong and that really left us super satisfied.

There is no parking available here, one has use the Pay and Parking place of the shopping mall just adjesannt to this place.

Overall, a must visit place if we happen to be in this area anytime. One may need to wait for tables, for its being occupied with people who are in no hurry while enjoying the food here!

**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Theeram recently with a friend, and it turned out to be a hidden gem for Kerala cuisine lovers—especially non-veg enthusiasts. However, there are a few things you should know before planning your visit.

The restaurant is located in a narrow lane of Kalina, Santacruz East, and does not have any dedicated parking, so you’ll need to manage that on your own. It’s a small, cozy place with limited seating—around four tables for four and two tables for two, so it’s not ideal for large groups. Ambience is simple, nothing fancy, but the focus here is clearly on food.

The menu is purely Kerala-style and is a treat for those who enjoy authentic regional flavors. However, it’s written in a local Kerala dialect/accent, which can be a bit tricky to understand. I recommend asking the staff to explain the dishes before you order.

We tried:
•	Seafood Soup – Flavorful, slightly spicy, and full of rich coastal taste. Highly recommend.
•	Tawa Prawns – Slightly undercooked/raw in texture, which I personally didn’t mind, but others may want to be cautious, especially those prone to allergies.
•	Fried Chicken – Crispy, but overly salty and quite oily. Not my favorite.
•	Egg Parotta – Soft, flaky, and tasty—this was a hit!
•	Shevaya Payasam – A perfect ending to the meal. Mild, sweet, and authentic.

The service was on the slower side, and a few items we wanted were unavailable, so we had to adjust our order based on what was available. That was a bit disappointing, but the flavors made up for it.
If you’re a non-veg lover or someone from Kerala missing homestyle food, this place is definitely worth a visit. Don’t expect a lavish setup—come for the food.
We’ll definitely be back, but a bit earlier next time to get the full menu experience.
